description:
In versions 1.0 and 1.1, all debit lines in a JournalEntryAdd request had to appear first, followed by all credit lines. But in versions 2.0 and above, the debit and credit lines can be intermingled. A credit line can legally come first in thejournal entry add.

The `journal_entry_add` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted. Returns the v2 request to send, and the webhook payload QuickBooks' answer arrives in (this operation's response_json: its data shape and the status codes to handle).

Possible errors (error.code / error.type; the call result explains each): 1030 unsupported_request, 3000 invalid_object_id, 3040 invalid_amount, 3070 string_too_long, 3120 object_not_found, 3140 invalid_reference, 3150 missing_element, 3175 in_use, 3176 locked, 3180 cannot_save, 3210 invalid_value, 3220 not_authorized, 3231 request_not_processed, 3250 feature_not_enabled, 3260 insufficient_permission, 3261 personal_data_access_denied, 3262 payroll_subscription_required, 3263 read_only_access, 3264 merchant_services_subscription_required, 3270 missing_posting_account

currency_ref.description:
A currency record defines how QuickBooks stores and displays a currency. Built-in currency name/code values are fixed; formatting and active status can vary by settings and workflow.

Choose at most one of: `is_home_currency_adjustment`, or the set (`currency_ref`, `exchange_rate`, `is_amounts_entered_in_home_currency`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

full_name.description: The record's name, parents first: `Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets`. Not case-sensitive.

list_id.description: QuickBooks' ID for the record. Used over `full_name` when both are sent.

def_macro.description: `def_macro` lets you assign a reusable name to a returned `txn_id` or `txn_line_id` so later requests can reference it with `useMacro`. This feature requires SDK 2.0+.

exchange_rate.description:
`exchange_rate` is the rate from this currency to the company’s home currency at AsOfDate. You can supply a rate when adding transactions, but QuickBooks does not provide rates through the SDK.

Choose at most one of: `is_home_currency_adjustment`, or the set (`currency_ref`, `exchange_rate`, `is_amounts_entered_in_home_currency`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

external_guid.description: Allows for the attachment of a user defined GUID value.

include_qbxml.description: Also return the qbXML this compiles to, for debugging. Not part of the v2 request.

is_adjustment.description: When a change is an “adjustment,” the original information is retained, usually so an accountant can see the effects of the adjustment.

is_amounts_entered_in_home_currency.description:
Flag that indicates the amount being entered is in the home currency.

Choose at most one of: `is_home_currency_adjustment`, or the set (`currency_ref`, `exchange_rate`, `is_amounts_entered_in_home_currency`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

is_home_currency_adjustment.description:
Indicates whether the transaction is using a home currency or foreign currency.

Choose at most one of: `is_home_currency_adjustment`, or the set (`currency_ref`, `exchange_rate`, `is_amounts_entered_in_home_currency`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

journal_credit_line.description:
If no amount is included in the first credit line (or debit line) of a journal entry in the QuickBooks user interface, then subsequent SDK queries on that JournalEntry object will fail XML validation.

At least one entry is required across `journal_debit_line` and `journal_credit_line`; they combine, any number of each. QuickBooks receives them in that order: every `journal_debit_line`, then every `journal_credit_line`.
